description:
Parse and resolve every user-supplied issue-id argument once in the CLI entry point, before any executor call, and retype the executor families that receive those ids so none of them parses or resolves an id again.

## Background

`main.rs` passes raw issue-id arguments from `cli.rs` to executor methods, which resolve them internally through `resolve_issue_id`. Internal callers such as template application and batch creation already hold full ids. `main.rs` holds 88 production issue-id references and truncates short ids with a literal length at `main.rs:3369,3769`. The short-hash tests at `crates/jit/tests/fast_issue/short_hash_tests.rs:156-220` drive executor methods with prefixes.

Resolving at the boundary alone leaves each executor method re-parsing the full id it receives, so the executor families that receive CLI ids are retyped here too. Those families hold several hundred production issue-id references and dozens of raw-id signatures, match ids inline (`commands/gate_check.rs`, `commands/validate.rs`), truncate short ids by length (`commands/graph.rs`, `commands/batch_create.rs`, `commands/validate.rs`), and resolve composite arguments inside the executor: `ArchiveTarget::Container` (`commands/archive.rs`), `DocumentScope::Issue` (`document/scope.rs`), `SnapshotScope::Issue` (`snapshot.rs`), and item-address issue segments (`domain/item.rs`, `commands/item.rs`, matched by hand in `validation/repository.rs`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Each plain issue-id argument that `main.rs` passes to the executor is parsed once into `IssueIdPrefix` and resolved once to `IssueId` before the call, `issue delete` included: it resolves before its deletion-confirmation check, and the failure-lever registry arm for that check seeds the issue it deletes.
- [hard] REQ-02: `cli.rs` argument structs keep raw strings only for values `main.rs` parses, and no other module parses a CLI issue-id argument.
- [hard] REQ-03: Too-short prefixes report the invalid-prefix error, and other malformed or unknown ids keep the not-found error class and exit code 3.
- [hard] REQ-04: Short ids rendered by `main.rs` come only from `short_id()`, and no site there truncates an id by length.
- [hard] REQ-05: Tests that exercise short-prefix input exercise it through the CLI entry point or the resolver, not through executor methods.
- [hard] REQ-06: `main.rs` holds no interim call-site parse: each issue-id argument is parsed exactly once, at the boundary.
- [hard] REQ-07: `ArchiveTarget::Container`, `DocumentScope::Issue` and `SnapshotScope::Issue` hold `IssueId`, resolved once in the CLI entry point before the executor call.
- [hard] REQ-08: Item-address issue segments hold `IssueIdPrefix`, parsed when an address is parsed from input or decoded from a document, and resolved through the shared resolver; the hand-written `starts_with` match is gone, and each consumer of an item-address issue segment, including the scope comparison at `validation/graph.rs:140`, compares through `IssueIdPrefix`.

- [hard] REQ-09: No struct field, enum field or function parameter in a family file (the family files are listed under Notes) holds an issue id as `String`, `&str` or `Vec<String>`; each uses `IssueId`. Template placeholder ids, which are not issue ids, keep their own type.
- [hard] REQ-10: Executor methods in these families take `&IssueId` and resolve no prefixes; dependency removal takes the source as `&IssueId` and its targets as `&[IssueId]` and compares them exactly with the source issue's own dependency list, so a dangling dependency can still be removed. Callers that hold full ids, such as templates, batch creation and tests, pass them directly.
- [hard] REQ-11: The CLI resolves each dependency-removal target once, against the source issue's own dependency ids, through the shared resolver, rejecting an ambiguous prefix.
- [hard] REQ-12: No production `IssueIdPrefix` parse and no production `resolve_issue_id` call remains in a family file, except the item-address resolution in `commands/item.rs`; the issue-id filters of `events query` and `claim status` pass their boundary-parsed prefix so records of a deleted issue still match.
- [hard] REQ-13: No inline or hand-written id-prefix match remains in a family file, and short ids there come only from `short_id()`; no site truncates an id by length.
- [hard] REQ-14: Code in these families, their unit-test modules included, uses issue ids only through `as_str()`, `short_id()`, `Display`, `Debug`, `Clone`, `PartialEq`/`Eq`, `PartialOrd`/`Ord`, `Hash` and serde, so it compiles unchanged once `IssueId` is the validated newtype.

## Notes

The families are: issue lifecycle (`commands/issue.rs`, `commands/claim.rs`, `commands/labels.rs`, `commands/events.rs`, `commands/bulk_update.rs`, `search.rs`, `query_engine/`); dependency (`commands/dependency.rs`, `commands/graph.rs`, `commands/template.rs`, `commands/template_expand.rs`, `commands/batch_create.rs`); gate (`commands/gate.rs`, `commands/gate_check.rs`, `gate_execution.rs`); executor core (`commands/mod.rs`, `commands/test_helpers.rs`); document (`commands/document.rs`, `commands/archive.rs`, `commands/item.rs`, `commands/validate.rs`).

`crate::domain::identity::IssueId` is at this point an alias for `String`, and the `IssueIdStaging` trait gives it `short_id()`. Retyping to the alias is compiler-neutral, so this change is checked by its criteria rather than by type errors; a later change replaces the alias with the validated newtype and the compiler then reports any site missed here. The shared integration-test harness is retyped separately; suite callers that hold `String` ids pass them as `&IssueId` unchanged under the alias.
title: The CLI resolves each issue-id argument once at entry
